outcome: Since 26 January 2024 the ring-of-integers form of the problem has been answered negatively for every number field K by two independent human-authored papers (Koymans and Pagano, preprint 2 Dec 2024; Alpöge, Bhargava, Ho and Shnidman, preprint 30 Jan 2025, published in Inventiones Mathematicae 2026), while the field itself has been claimed undecidable only for K = Q, by an unrefereed OpenAI manuscript of 6 Oct 2026 with no Lean formalisation and no qualified check on record; no field-level result for any other number field was found.
problem_asks: The bullet reads 'For which number fields does Hilbert's tenth problem hold?'. 'Hold' is read as the negative answer, that no algorithm decides solvability. The bullet does not say whether 'Hilbert's tenth problem for K' means solvability over the ring of integers O_K or over the field K itself, so both readings are listed. (a) Ring reading: for which number fields K is solvability in O_K of polynomial equations with integer-ring coefficients undecidable? (b) Field reading: for which number fields K is solvability over K itself of polynomial equations with coefficients in K undecidable? Under (a), K = Q is already the classical case, since O_Q = Z and Hilbert's tenth problem over Z is undecidable by Matiyasevich (1970). Under (b), K = Q is the open rational case, and the bullet asks about every other number field K as well. The bullet names no particular class of fields, so the answer is either a class of fields or all of them, under each reading.

events.what_happened: Peter Koymans and Carlo Pagano post 'Hilbert's tenth problem via additive combinatorics' (arXiv:2412.01768, v1 2 Dec 2024). Main theorem as read in the abstract: 'For all infinite rings R that are finitely generated over Z, we show that Hilbert's tenth problem has a negative answer.' Theorem 1.2 as read in the arXiv HTML: for every number field K, Z is Diophantine over the ring of integers O_K; Theorem 1.1 follows from Theorem 1.2 by Eisentraeger's thesis. Method as described in the abstract and talks: elliptic curves with full rational 2-torsion, 2-descent, and additive-combinatorics input. Quanta (3 Feb 2025) and the Wikipedia article (as read) describe it as a preprint with a claimed proof.
events.revisions: v1 2 Dec 2024; v2 22 Apr 2025; v3 24 Nov 2025 (comment: 'Details added in various sections'). The arXiv page lists no journal reference. Companion expository preprint arXiv:2602.04468 is a separate event.
events.delivers: A negative answer to Hilbert's tenth problem over O_K for every number field K (ring reading), and over every infinite ring finitely generated over Z. Restriction: the theorem concerns rings. It does not address the field K itself. Q is not finitely generated as a ring over Z, so the rational field is not covered by the stated theorem, although O_Q = Z is.
events.remains: Field reading: undecidability of solvability over the field K itself is not addressed by these theorems, for any number field, including K = Q. Ring reading: on the published statement, nothing remains for the number fields in the bullet, subject to the proof being correct, which is the open question here.

events.what_happened: Levent Alpöge, Manjul Bhargava, Wei Ho and Ari Shnidman post 'Rank stability in quadratic extensions and Hilbert's tenth problem for the ring of integers of a number field' (arXiv:2501.18774, 30 Jan 2025, 10 pages; the only version listed). Theorem 1.1 as read: for any quadratic extension of number fields K/F there is an abelian variety A/F with rank A(F) = rank A(K) > 0. Corollary 1.2 as read: Z has a diophantine model over O_K, so Hilbert's tenth problem has a negative solution over O_K, for every number field K. Published: Inventiones Mathematicae 243(3) (March 2026), pp. 1129-1139, first online 1 Dec 2025, DOI 10.1007/s00222-025-01392-3, according to a Nature Index record and a Hebrew University listing seen in search results. I could not open the Springer page itself. Quanta (3 Feb 2025) reports this as a second, independent proof posted less than two months after Koymans and Pagano.
events.revisions: arXiv v1 30 Jan 2025, the only version listed. Journal version Inventiones 243(3), March 2026, first online 1 Dec 2025.
events.delivers: A negative answer to Hilbert's tenth problem over O_K for every number field K (ring reading), through a diophantine model of Z over O_K. The key input is a rank-stability statement for quadratic extensions, proved by existence of an abelian variety, so the object is non-constructive. Restriction: the ring reading only. The field K itself is not addressed. Q is covered as a ring, O_Q = Z.
events.remains: Field reading: undecidability over the field K itself is not addressed, for any number field including K = Q. Ring reading: nothing remains for the number fields in the bullet.

events.what_happened: Bjorn Poonen posts 'Rank stability makes rings of integers diophantine' (arXiv:2510.19553, 22 Oct 2025, 6 pages, single author). As summarised from the abstract: a recent negative answer to Hilbert's tenth problem over rings of integers relies on a theorem about number field extensions L/K, namely that if an abelian variety over K has positive rank over K equal to its rank over L, then the ring of integers of K is diophantine over the ring of integers of L. The note gives an alternative proof of this theorem and reviews how it is used.
events.revisions: v1 22 Oct 2025 (the only version I saw). No journal reference listed.
events.delivers: An alternative proof of a supporting rank-stability theorem for number field extensions. It does not establish undecidability for any number field by itself; it supports the chain of reasoning used in the ring-of-integers results.
events.remains: Nothing new for the bullet. The status of every case is unchanged by this note.
events.direction: Consistent with the negative answer over O_K; it does not change the direction of any other event.

events.what_happened: Yuri Matiyasevich and Zhi-Wei Sun post 'Undecidability on Diophantine equations over Z[i] with 20 unknowns' (arXiv:2510.18794, 21 Oct 2025, 9 pages). As read from the abstract page: no algorithm decides solvability over Z[i], the ring of Gaussian integers, for integer polynomial equations in 20 variables. The abstract states this improves a previous record of 52 variables (Matiyasevich and Sun, 2017; see the predates entry).

events.remains: Nothing about the set of number fields. The field reading for Q(i) is not addressed by this result.
events.direction: Cuts toward undecidability over Z[i], with a smaller variable count. Consistent with the negative reading for Q(i). It is a neighbour of the bullet, not a new field.

events.what_happened: Tobias Boege, Anna Hofer and Thomas Kahle post 'Trinomial containment in polynomial ideals is undecidable' (arXiv:2608.31162, math.AC, v1 31 Aug 2026, 16 pages). Deciding whether an ideal in a polynomial ring contains a trinomial is undecidable. From an integer polynomial P they build an ideal whose trinomial containment is equivalent to P having an integral zero, and then use the MRDP theorem. This is a result about polynomial ideals, not about number fields. The introduction's subsection 'AI in this research' (as read through the arXiv HTML summary) says: 'In the end it was GPT 5.6 Sol (OpenAI) which came up with the first valid proof in July 2026.' It also says 'Next to GPT 5.6 Sol, also Claude Fable 5 (Anthropic) was used.' and 'Finally, a Lean formalization of our proof was almost entirely generated by coding agents.' The abstract does not mention AI.
events.delivers: Undecidability of trinomial containment in polynomial ideals, using Hilbert's tenth problem over Z as input. It does not concern number fields or rings of integers of number fields.
events.remains: Nothing about the bullet. It is recorded because it is an AI-credited result on a neighbouring problem that uses the classical integer result.

events.what_happened: OpenAI posts 'Hilbert's tenth problem over the rational numbers' as one manuscript in the openai/math collection of 722 press-reported manuscripts (the README and CONTENTS.md give 719 manuscripts in 372 families; the discrepancy is not reconciled). The LaTeX source (build/main.tex) gives the main claim in the abstract: 'We give a negative answer to Hilbert's tenth problem over the rational numbers: no algorithm decides whether a polynomial with integer coefficients has a rational zero', with 'The number of variables is part of the input.' The argument, as read through summarising fetches of build/sections/01 to 07, is a reduction from integer solvability to rational solvability. Assuming an algorithm for rational solvability, it builds for each integer polynomial f a finite family of rational tests from a recursive first-order theory over an elliptic curve E: y^2 = x^3 - d^2 x over F = Q(sqrt 2), with d = 75 - 53 sqrt 2, which the paper says has rank 1 over F (Proposition 1, two-isogeny descent, citing Silverman and Poonen 2002). Section 03 builds a positive existential formula over Q (pole parity), using two-descent on curves y^2 = x(x - l)(x + 3l). Section 04 proves a height bound for rational points via a genus-5 Shimura curve and modularity. Section 06 proves prime-pattern lemmas using Green-Tao-Ziegler. Section 07 concludes that H10(Q) has Turing degree 0', the degree of the halting problem, and that no bound is imposed on the number of variables. The paper states that Mazur's conjecture would rule out a Diophantine definition of Z in Q, that these obstructions 'do not by themselves rule out a negative answer', and that the construction gives no single existential definition of Z in Q. The paper names no AI system, model, agent or prompt, and no human discoverer. Its only author line is 'OpenAI'.
events.revisions: Two dated directories exist in openai/math: 'Hilberts-tenth-problem-over-the-rational-numbers-September-24-2026' (README: 'Date: September 24, 2026'; its only commit is 'Initial commit', 6 Oct 2026, SHA adc7f12) and 'Hilberts-tenth-problem-over-the-rational-numbers-October-6-2026' (README: 'updates citations to revised manuscripts in this collection', and links to the September 24 version). The repository's public appearance is therefore 6 Oct 2026; the author-dated version is 24 Sep 2026, which I could not independently date. I have recorded the public date as the date of the event. The judging pass can take the author date instead.
events.delivers: A negative answer for the field Q: no algorithm decides rational solvability of integer polynomial equations, for any number of variables. The claimed strength is H10(Q) of Turing degree 0'. Restriction: the rational field Q only. The paper states that it does not establish that Z is Diophantine over Q, so the standard route through Diophantine definability of Z over Q is not what the reduction uses. Under the ring reading, Q is already classical (O_Q = Z), so this adds nothing there.
events.remains: Field reading for every number field K other than Q: not addressed. Under the field reading for Q, nothing remains if the claim is correct; the claim itself is unverified (see doubts). Lean formalisation and human checking are both absent.
events.doubts: (1) Not peer-reviewed and not Lean-formalised. The repository's CONTENTS.md gives family 004 with no Lean link, lean/formalization.yaml has no entry for this result, and Gasarch (11 Oct 2026) writes 'It has not been Lean-formalized.' Commentary I found does not describe any completed check. The Galois representations digest (8 Oct 2026, Persiflage) says the result 'threw me for a loop' and hopes a colleague will write a guest post; Gasarch (11 Oct 2026) writes 'I will assume their proof is correct.' (2) The argument depends on two companion preprints from the same unreviewed collection, cited by key in the bibliography as 'PointwiseTwoConverse' (openai/math, 'A-pointwise-2-converse-for-elliptic-curves-with-rational-two-torsion-October-7-2026') and 'OddRegularFontaineMazurAtTwo' (openai/math, 'Fontaine-Mazur-modularity-at-the-prime-2-October-6-2026'). Neither was read. (3) As read through summarising fetches of the LaTeX sections (not verbatim, so verify before relying on them): section 06 states the lower bound as 'We claim that' and depends on a Green-Tao-Ziegler asymptotic, with the 2024 erratum described as leaving that inverse theorem unchanged; section 05 says Proposition 2 'applies verbatim' to the conjugate equation; section 04 says the CM-case finiteness 'need not be effective'; section 02 uses an external convex-subgroup valuation step described as sketched; section 03 says 'no sufficiency is being asserted'. (4) OpenAI's own release notes that 'some of the unformalized results could have issues', and in the same release three papers on Weil classes and the rational Hodge conjecture were withdrawn for a sign error (not this manuscript). (5) A blog commenter alleges the paper cites Jennifer Park's work 'in a completely wrong way'. I could not find Park's post or the passage, so this is unverified. (6) The date is disputed as between the September 24 directory and the October 6 public posting. The window is unaffected either way.
events.direction: Cuts toward undecidability, which is the bullet's 'holds' reading, for the field Q if the claim holds. This is the only field-level claim found for any number field.

events.what_happened: Poonen, 'Using elliptic curves of rank one towards the undecidability of Hilbert's Tenth Problem over rings of algebraic integers', Algorithmic Number Theory (ANTS-V, Sydney, July 2002), arXiv math/0204001 (April 2002). Per the search summaries: if an elliptic curve E over Q has rank 1 over both Q and a number field K, then Z has a diophantine definition over O_K, so Hilbert's tenth problem is negative over O_K. The main theorem reduces the Denef-Lipshitz conjecture to a plausible conjecture about the existence of such curves.

events.what_happened: Manuscript 'Hilbert's tenth problem over the rational numbers' (main.tex, dated October 6, 2026) claims Theorem thm:main: no algorithm, given f in Z[X_1,...,X_n] with n part of the input, decides whether f has a zero in Q^n. The proof builds, for nonconstant f, a computable sequence of finite rational-solvability tests such that f has an integer zero if and only if every test succeeds. Its ingredients are a rank-one elliptic curve over F = Q(sqrt 2) supplying integer indices (Proposition ell:rank), a five-point height estimate (Theorem hei:height), a pole-parity positive existential formula obtained from two-descent (Proposition par:pole-parity), and prime-pattern lemmas. Corollary thm:degree-normal-form adds that the rational problem has Turing degree 0', and that the same holds for integer polynomials of total degree at most four and for sums of squares of degree at most two, with no bound on the number of variables. The other manuscript, 'A pointwise 2-converse for elliptic curves with rational two-torsion', is not about Hilbert's tenth problem; the Hilbert manuscript cites its Theorem 1.1 as an input (see conditional_on).
events.revisions: 2 earlier edition(s) kept in the repository: Hilberts-tenth-problem-over-the-rational-numbers-September-24-2026, A-pointwise-2-converse-for-elliptic-curves-with-rational-two-torsion-September-24-2026
events.delivers: Settles the case K = Q, negatively: solvability over Q of integer polynomials is undecidable, with the number of variables part of the input. Field reading (K is the field the unknowns range over): K = Q is the open rational case, and this is the one case of the bullet the manuscript decides. Ring reading (solvability in the ring of integers O_K): K = Q is Matiyasevich's 1970 theorem, so nothing new there. The manuscripts make no claim about any other number field K, either as a field or through its ring of integers. The proof is over Q; Q(sqrt 2) appears only as an auxiliary field for the elliptic curve. The introduction cites results for other K (Koymans and Pagano 2026, and Alpoge, Bhargava, Ho and Shnidman 2026, for the ring of integers of every number field; Poonen; Mazur and Rubin, conditionally) as background, not as claims of this family. So the manuscripts do not identify a class of number fields, and do not claim to answer the bullet as worded.
events.remains: Field reading: for every number field K other than Q, whether solvability over K itself is undecidable; the manuscripts neither say which K are undecidable nor say that their method extends. Ring reading: for every K other than Q, nothing in these manuscripts. The manuscripts also state that their restricted corollaries are Turing-equivalent results, not many-one completeness, and that the construction gives no single existential definition of Z in Q.
events.doubts: The text flags no step as sketched and contains no hedge about the main theorem. The abstract and Theorem thm:main agree. The main limits are the ones the text itself states: the restricted corollaries are Turing-degree statements only, and the construction gives no bound on the number of variables and no single existential definition of Z in Q. The argument is written in an elementary-extension and compactness style, with transfer principles used in the key divisibility and height steps. Its dependence on the 2-converse manuscript and on the Fontaine-Mazur preprint is as described above. I checked the statements and the main assembly, not every proof step.; conditional on: (i) The pole-parity step (Section 03, Lemma par:global-point) uses Theorem 1.1 of the pointwise 2-converse manuscript to get finiteness of Sha(E_l/Q) for curves E_l with full rational two-torsion and 2^infinity-Selmer corank at most one. The Cassels-Tate pairing argument is written out in the text. (ii) The modularity step of the height estimate (Section 04) uses the odd regular Fontaine-Mazur theorem at 2, cited as Theorem 1.1 of the OpenAI preprint 'Fontaine-Mazur modularity at the prime 2' (October 6, 2026). That preprint is outside this family and I did not read it; the text states that its hypotheses are verified for the representation at hand. (iii) The prime-pattern lemma (Section 06) uses the Green-Tao-Ziegler inverse theorem, cited with a 2024 erratum that the text says leaves the stated inverse theorem unchanged. (iv) Other cited published results include Faltings, Bost, Zarhin, von Kaenel and Kret, Silverman, and Davis-Putnam-Robinson-Matiyasevich.
events.direction: proves undecidability for K = Q only (negative answer over the rational field); no class of number fields

disputes.summary: A commenter on the Galois representations digest (Maarten Derickx) alleges the OpenAI paper cites Jennifer Park's work in a completely wrong way, and points to a Park post. Another commenter disputes that the point is cogent. I could not locate Park's post or the passage in the manuscript, so the allegation is unverified.

Koymans-Pagano (Dec 2024) and Alpöge-Bhargava-Ho-Shnidman (Jan 2025) both claim the negative answer over rings of integers of every number field, by different methods, within two months of each other. Quanta presents them as two independent proofs of the same result. No priority dispute between them was found in the sources read.

summary: Ring reading (rings of integers O_K, which includes K = Q through Z): two papers claim a negative answer for every number field. Koymans and Pagano (arXiv:2412.01768, first posted 2 Dec 2024; v3 Nov 2025) prove that Z is Diophantine over O_K for every number field K, and hence that Hilbert's tenth problem is negative for every infinite ring finitely generated over Z. I read the abstract and the first 100000 of about 178000 characters of the arXiv HTML; the remainder is appendix and references. Alpöge, Bhargava, Ho and Shnidman (arXiv:2501.18774, 30 Jan 2025) reach the same conclusion by a different route, through a rank-stability theorem for quadratic extensions, and this paper is published in Inventiones Mathematicae 243(3), pp. 1129-1139, online 1 Dec 2025, which I could confirm only through a Nature Index record and a Hebrew University listing, not the Springer page. Poonen (arXiv:2510.19553, Oct 2025) gives an alternative proof of a rank-stability theorem that these results rely on. Koymans and Pagano have no journal listing I could confirm. The OpenAI bibliography and a tracker both say JAMS, forthcoming, but this is unverified. Close call for the ring reading: whether the published ABHS paper alone is enough to count the ring reading as settled, or whether the preprint status of Koymans-Pagano matters. Field reading (solvability over the field K itself): the only claim found for any number field is OpenAI's repository manuscript 'Hilbert's tenth problem over the rational numbers', dated 24 Sep 2026 by its author and first publicly posted 6 Oct 2026. Its LaTeX states that no algorithm decides rational solvability of integer polynomial equations, and that H10(Q) has Turing degree 0', using a reduction from integer solvability with an elliptic curve of rank 1 over Q(sqrt 2). The paper claims no Diophantine definition of Z over Q. It has no Lean formalisation in the repository's catalogue, no human verification in the sources, two companion preprints from the same collection that it cites by key, and several steps that are flagged in the text as sketched or hedged (as read through summaries, to be checked). Gasarch and the Galois representations digest both state that they have not verified it. For every other number field K the field reading is open in my sources; the ring results do not transfer to K without an existential definition of O_K over K, which my sources describe as open for Q and most fields. AI involvement: the OpenAI manuscript names no system, and the repository's README credits an 'unreleased internal OpenAI model' for the collection as a whole; no per-result statement exists, so it is recorded as the authors' batch-level account. The Koymans-Pagano and ABHS papers name no AI in the parts I read. Ding-Li (arXiv:2606.12776, 11 Jun 2026) calls its Z[i] result 'an AI proof' without naming a system. Trinomial containment (Boege-Hofer-Kahle, arXiv:2608.31162, 31 Aug 2026) names GPT 5.6 Sol (OpenAI) and Claude Fable 5 (Anthropic) on a neighbouring problem that is not about number fields. Pre-2024 milestones, recorded as predates entries, establish the classical partial results (Denef and Denef-Lipshitz for totally real and related fields, Pheidas and Shapiro-Shlapentokh for other classes, Poonen's rank-one elliptic-curve method, Mazur-Rubin's conditional result, and García-Fritz-Pasten's and Kundu-Lei-Sprung's families). These are secondary-source dates, not checked against originals. Close call on the reading of the bullet: 'hold' is read as undecidability, and the bullet does not say whether it means rings or fields; both readings are carried in problem_asks, and the later pass should decide which the bullet means.
competing_reading: Count the ring reading as settled: ABHS is published in Inventiones, and Koymans-Pagano is a preprint whose main theorem covers every number field. On that view the bullet is answered as 'all number fields', and the OpenAI manuscript is a neighbouring claim about the field Q that does not change that answer. The opposite reading treats the bullet as the field question and sets the ring results aside: only Q has a claim, the claim is unverified, and so nothing field-level is established for any number field. A third reading takes Koymans-Pagano as unpublished, which would leave the ring reading resting on one published paper (ABHS) plus the Koymans-Pagano preprint.
what_would_settle_it: For the ring reading: confirmation that Koymans and Pagano's paper is accepted at JAMS or another journal, and a check that the Inventiones version of ABHS has the same main theorem as the arXiv v1. For the field reading: an expert check or Lean formalisation of the OpenAI rational reduction, including the two companion preprints it depends on (PointwiseTwoConverse and Fontaine-Mazur at 2) and the Green-Tao-Ziegler lower-bound step; and a result showing whether O_K is existentially definable over K for number fields other than Q. The most direct check is the Lean repository for the OpenAI result, which is absent now. Also: the Wikipedia article's own wording, to settle whether the bullet means rings or fields.

Its argument and quotations come from summarising fetches of the LaTeX section files, and the summaries are paraphrases with some quoted phrases. Every quotation from that source, including the README sentence in ai.systems, must be checked verbatim before anyone relies on it. The two companion preprints the manuscript depends on (the pointwise 2-converse, Oct 7 2026, and Fontaine-Mazur at 2, Oct 6 2026) were not read, and neither was the reasoning-trace material for family 004. (2) The Koymans-Pagano v3 HTML was read only through its first 100000 of about 178000 characters; the remainder (appendix and references) was not read. ABHS was read from its v1 HTML only. (3) Journal status: the ABHS Inventiones publication and its date come from search-result records (Nature Index, Hebrew University listing), not the Springer page. The Koymans-Pagano JAMS status rests on the OpenAI bibliography and a tracker, and I could not confirm it. event.what_happened: Levent Alpöge, Manjul Bhargava, Wei Ho and Ari Shnidman post 'Rank stability in quadratic extensions and Hilbert's tenth problem for the ring of integers of a number field' (arXiv:2501.18774, 30 Jan 2025, 10 pages; the only version listed). Theorem 1.1 as read: for any quadratic extension of number fields K/F there is an abelian variety A/F with rank A(F) = rank A(K) > 0. Corollary 1.2 as read: Z has a diophantine model over O_K, so Hilbert's tenth problem has a negative solution over O_K, for every number field K. Published: Inventiones Mathematicae 243(3) (March 2026), pp. 1129-1139, first online 1 Dec 2025, DOI 10.1007/s00222-025-01392-3, according to a Nature Index record and a Hebrew University listing seen in search results. I could not open the Springer page itself. Quanta (3 Feb 2025) reports this as a second, independent proof posted less than two months after Koymans and Pagano.
event.revisions: arXiv v1 30 Jan 2025, the only version listed. Journal version Inventiones 243(3), March 2026, first online 1 Dec 2025.
event.delivers: A negative answer to Hilbert's tenth problem over O_K for every number field K (ring reading), through a diophantine model of Z over O_K. The key input is a rank-stability statement for quadratic extensions, proved by existence of an abelian variety, so the object is non-constructive. Restriction: the ring reading only. The field K itself is not addressed. Q is covered as a ring, O_Q = Z.
event.remains: Field reading: undecidability over the field K itself is not addressed, for any number field including K = Q. Ring reading: nothing remains for the number fields in the bullet.

judgement.why: The decisive call is the reading of the bullet. 'Hilbert's tenth problem for a number field' in the list's context is the Denef-Lipshitz question about rings of integers O_K (the classes Denef, Pheidas, Shapiro-Shlapentokh, Poonen etc. are all ring results, and K=Q is then Matiyasevich). On that reading Koymans-Pagano and Alpöge-Bhargava-Ho-Shnidman each answer the whole question ('all number fields'); ABHS is accepted in Inventiones (digested), Koymans-Pagano remains a preprint with only Poonen's work on a supporting theorem, so unreviewed. The OpenAI rational-field manuscript (recorded twice, as openai-hilbert-q-2026-10 and openai-math-004) addresses the field Q, a different question under the ring reading, so it is a variant; even under the field reading it would be only a case (Q alone). Variable-count improvements (Matiyasevich-Sun, Ding-Li, Sun) and the trinomial paper do not change which fields are covered and are variants. Conditional results (Mazur-Rubin, Murty-Pasten) and tools/expository/alternative proofs of supporting lemmas are none. Pre-snapshot class results are cases; Poonen 2003 and Mazur-Rubin-Shlapentokh concern subrings of Q / definability over Q and are variants.
judgement.doubts: If the bullet is instead read as the field question, the ring results become variants and the OpenAI Q claim becomes the only after-snapshot case (AI-generated per a batch-level README quote, unreviewed). The OpenAI AI credit rests on a collection-wide README sentence rather than a per-manuscript statement. Ding-Li call their proof 'an AI proof' but name no system, so ai.systems is empty and it is scored none; it is a variant either way. Journal status of ABHS comes from search-result records, not the Springer page; pre-2024 publication facts are secondary.
